content.thinking:
I'm planning the kitsune fox design in full before writing the file since I can't typecheck as I go—imagining a fox roughly 0.8m at the shoulder with a 1.3m body, nine tails fanning out behind with spirit flames glowing at their tips, rendered in a cel-shaded anime style.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton coordinates for the spine, neck, and hip joints, setting up chain hierarchies so the spine connects to the hips and the neck chains off the spine's last joint.

Then I define the head and jaw joints with specific positions and orientations, and start sweeping the body mesh along the spine chain using radius profiles for the geometry.

Working out the fox's torso proportions...

For the color palette, I'm picturing a classic Inari kitsune look: pale cream-white fur with lavender shadow tones, crimson facial markings, gold ornaments, and cyan-violet spirit flames for the tails.

Working out how to shade the coat and legs — darker indigo stockings fading into crimson "socks" near the paws, with a crimson zigzag pattern along the spine suggesting fur-tipped markings rather than a solid stripe.

Now moving to the head: building the skull as a scaled sphere, snout as a loft shape, extruded triangle ears with crimson insides, and cheek fur ruffs using tufted textures tinted cream-to-lavender for a toon cel look. I'm placing decal eyes directly onto the skull surface, following the usual pattern for positioning head decals.

For eyes, I'm going with slanted fox-style shapes using gold irises to contrast against the blue flames, sized small to match the compact skull proportions, angled forward around ±38° azimuth with decals placed at the hit point. Now I'm sweeping a tapered loft from the skull front to the nose to form the snout shape.

Adding small details: a dark sphere for the nose tip, a jaw sweep for the lower jaw colored cream, and tiny white fang spikes on the upper and lower jaw bones. For the ears, I'm extruding a triangular outline positioned at the ear base on each side, drawn in the front-facing plane with points defining the tip shape.

Setting the ear thickness and tilt so the extrusion direction points forward, then adding a smaller crimson inner-ear shape offset slightly outward. I'm making the ears large for a kitsune look and adding a small gold earring torus at the ear base, then starting work on the leg placements beginning with the front shoulder position.

Working out leg IK chains...

I'll use polyline chains for the legs with smooth sweep rounding the corners, calling b.chain with the raw points and parent/name/role options -- front legs parenting off the spine's last joint, hind legs off the hip root. For sides, s=1 is left and s=-1 is right, with names suffixed L or R accordingly.

Now I'm defining leg sweep radii with tapering profiles, giving the front legs a thinner taper and the hind thighs a thicker haunch near the top, and painting dark sock colors with a cel-shaded gradient below a certain height threshold. I'm also shaping the paws as scaled spheres at the leg tips with sock coloring and toe details.

Adding claw spikes and tails...

Computing each tail's curve direction and length, bending points upward progressively toward the tip, with center tails longest; checking that overall height stays around 1.9m, which seems tall but plausible.

Adjusting elevation angle and lift values to around 1.6m peak plus flame height, which feels reasonable, and adding a slight outward curl to tail tips via the horizontal offset term already baked into the direction vector.

Setting up the tail joint chain attached at the hip/root joint with role "tail" and four segments each.

I'm fixing the naming scheme since tail0 and tail1 joint numbers could collide — switching to `tail${k}_` with an underscore separator so joints like tail0_1 stay unambiguous under the allowed naming regex.

For the tail's shape, I'm defining a radius function that starts fluffy, tapers to a point near the tip, and layering in a color transition from white body to a crimson/fire-colored tip using a gradient sampled along the path.

Making gold rings around the tail using a closed catmull sweep with eight points each, then adding spirit flame wisps at each tail tip using cross-card billboards with a glowing flame texture so they read well from any viewing angle.

I need to orient each flame card to face upward along the tangent at the tail's tip, binding it to the last joint in the tail chain so it follows the bone properly, and I'm also adding a small glowing blue-core sphere at each tip for extra fire effect.

For the flame texture itself, I'm layering simple teardrop-shaped SVG paths (outer, mid, core) with flat colors instead of gradients to keep rendering safe, alternating between a blue palette and a violet palette across the nine flames for variety.

I'm also adding floating hitodama orbs orbiting the fox—small glowing spheres paired with flame cards, attached to the hip bone and arranged in a ring at varying heights and radius so they hover around without affecting the character's standing height. For the gold trim, I'm sweeping a closed bead ring around the neck for a necklace and adding hanging tassel beads along strands.

Instead of a plain collar, I'm thinking a shimenawa-style twisted rope wrapped around the neck, painted with straw-gold and crimson stripes, plus shide zigzag paper strips hanging off it as small white extruded slabs for that shrine aesthetic.

For the hanging cards I need to fix their orientation so they face outward with correct bone attachment to the neck joint rather than defaulting upward. I also want to add a decal for a crimson diamond forehead marking, placing it via a raycast hit on the skull with a tilted normal direction.

Now I'm adding Kumadori-style cheek stripes as decals using mirrored SVG line textures on both sides of the face, plus building a chest ruff with cream fur tuft cards using a layered SVG path shape for shading.

I'm setting up scatter filters for the cheek and neck ruff, using surface normal and position checks to place fur cards only on the cheek and chest areas with appropriate size, lean, and flow direction.

I'm also planning decorative flame-swirl decals on the haunches, positioning them symmetrically on each side of the body surface.

Now I'm working out gold anklet rings for the front legs, calculating ring radius relative to leg taper, then moving on to designing a gold crescent circlet for the forehead.

Fixing the torus orientation by rotating it so its axis aligns with Y. For the tails, I'm adding crimson tips, gold rings, and flame accents, plus a fur-edge treatment contrasting lavender and white along the tail's length for stylized shading.

I decide to skip the tuft-card streaks along the tails since getting the orientation right is tricky, keeping them clean with just the rings and flame tip instead.

I'll split into two scatters: white tufts filtered far from the tip, and a separate crimson tuft texture filtered near the tip, needing a new tuft function with fill, shade, and stroke params. For whiskers, I'm planning thin rod sweeps from the muzzle, three per side with flat ends and a small radius.

Brow marks come free with the anime eye decal, so I can skip adding those separately, and I'll skip the tongue and mouth interior details for now. I'm adding crimson kumadori decals on the cheeks and forehead, and now working out the head's position and scale relative to the neck joint to figure out how the skull connects.

Now I'm placing the muzzle, jaw, and nose relative to the skull -- the eyes sit at the front-sides of the skull, the lower jaw sweeps forward to the chin in white cel coloring, and the nose tip gets a small dark sphere. I'm also deciding the muzzle stays coat-colored, the belly gets a lavender cel tone, and I'll add a hair tuft near the hips while skipping finer sector details.

I'm finishing the eye tail count at nine and adding hitodama orbs for the hands. For accessories, I'm designing gold ear tassels hanging crimson spheres from rods near the cheeks, plus a gold collar with eight crimson beads and a central pendant to layer alongside a possible shimenawa rope detail at the neck.

Working out where exactly to anchor that chest pendant is tricky — I'm trying different ways to find a stable point on the neck surface pointing forward, since ray casts toward the geometry might miss, so I'll settle on picking a nearest-point anchor just in front of the neck's centerline.

Placing a small flattened gold disc there with a gem as the pendant...

For the collar, I'm checking that the ring radius matches the neck's tapering radius at that point along the sweep, but rather than risk a mismatched ellipse-tube fit, I'll use the surface loop method tied to the neck joint's own bone axis so the collar drapes exactly along the curve.

With three neck joints at 0, 1/3, and 2/3, I'll place the collar at joint 1 with a slight lift, and use joint 0 (near the base) for the shimenawa rope so it sits lower rather than crowding near the head.

Working out the straw texture now, giving the rope a twisted appearance using striped coloring with warm tan tones.

Now I'm figuring out the shide paper streamers hanging from the rope—placing frames along the rope path, orienting them to hang downward, and sketching a zigzag paper outline for the traditional shape.

Now I'm setting up the module imports I'll need—builder, frame, path utilities, IK limbs, paint/texture helpers, and toon shading kit—then starting to define the color palette for fur and shading.

Still layering fur edges...

Now I'm setting up the spine chain with four joints resampled from a catmull curve running from hips to upper back, then defining the hips joint as the root of the spine hierarchy.

Next I'm sweeping the body profile with a sine-based radius curve for a tapered chest shape, then building the neck as a separate chain from upper spine up to the head position, using a shaded white-to-lavender fur edge color for the neck sweep.

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy: the neck parents off the final spine joint, the head parents off the final neck joint, and the tail parents off the hips, with each limb group built from four joints and totaling around thirty-six joints across the skeleton.

I'm also naming out the shoulder, elbow, and paw joints per limb (front legs 3 joints each, hind legs adding one more), tallying spine, neck, head, jaw, and hips joints, and adding simple hinge-style ear joints on the head for extra expressiveness, bringing the total to roughly sixty-two joints with room for additional orb or flame groups on the hips.

Working out the ear geometry now — placing the ear base point mirrored across the x-axis, figuring out the outward and tilt directions for each side, and computing the cross product to get the ear's thickness axis so I can offset the inner ear surface toward the front correctly for both left and right sides.

Defining ear outline points...

Now I'm setting up the extrude paint logic so the ear tip shades darker toward the point, then moving on to placing the hitodama orbs symmetrically around the front and sides, avoiding overlap with the tails.

I'll skip extra sparkle spheres for now and apply glow to the textured cards so they keep their tinted colors. For the tail flame, I'm framing a card at the tip point with a slight sink, sized narrow and tall, bound to the last tail joint, and considering whether a small glowing core sphere at the tip is even necessary since the crimson tip already reads well.

For the eye and cheek decals, I'm placing them using spherical coordinates around the head, mirroring the azimuth by side so the right eye markers land correctly, and sizing the crimson swoosh texture small so it reads as an outward-flowing mark near the outer corner of each eye.

Setting the skull radius for sizing, then placing a forehead decal shaped like a diamond/flame marking centered at the skull with a small size range. I'm also figuring out where to position a gem on the forehead relative to the eyes and the marking's elevation so it doesn't overlap awkwardly.

Positioning the gem stud at an elevation below the forehead mark with a small glowing sphere and gold torus ring, then sketching out the whisker rods extending outward from the muzzle with thin radii and light coloring.

Now I'm adding fangs as bone-attached spikes near the mouth corners, upper ones pointing down and lower ones pointing up, and starting to plan haunch marking decals using a surface element on the body.

I'm reconsidering decal placement since the hind leg sweep near the haunch would partially hide a swirl there, so I'm thinking of relocating one marking to the shoulder area above the front leg and keeping another near the haunch at a different elevation to avoid overlap.

For the leg thickness, I'm shaping tapered radius profiles for both hind and front legs using smooth keyed values that thin out from thick at the top to narrow near the foot.

For leg coloring, I'm painting a sock pattern where the lower portion of the leg gets one color and the upper part another, using a zigzag function based on position so the boundary between colors isn't a flat line but has a jagged transition.

Now I'm shaping the paws as small flattened spheres colored to match the sock, positioned at the foot of each leg, then adding small claw spikes in ivory at the front of each paw angled slightly downward and outward to look like toes. I'm double-checking that the paw positions line up correctly with where each leg chain ends.

For the hind legs, I'm setting up the knee to bend forward and the hock to bend backward, giving a natural two-joint leg with three segments. For the front legs, I'm using a single elbow bend pointing backward with two segments, making sure the root-to-target geometry and plane orientation work out properly.

I'm figuring out the leg lengths so they're slightly longer than the straight-line distance to the target, avoiding degenerate fully-extended poses while keeping the bend subtle. I'm also working out how each limb's chain gets built from an array of points, with named joints for the shoulder/elbow/paw on front legs and hip/knee/hock/paw on hind legs, each parented appropriately to the spine.

Now I'm scattering fur tufts across different body regions using surface sampling with directional filters: neck ruff pointing downward on the underside, chest tufts on the front-facing lower body, and cheek ruffs on the sides of the skull, each with its own flow direction and density settings to vary the fur's lean and spin.

For the tail, I'm adding separate scatters for white and crimson tufts split by distance from the tip, flowing toward the tail's direction vector with slightly larger card sizes, and tallying up the total card count across all these scatters to keep things reasonable.

Skipping the old bell idea for tail five. I'm considering a gold forehead crescent instead of a full kanzashi crown, setting up the anime eye with a golden iris and pink blush, and keeping all painted parts on one shared paint sheet. I'm also defining the SVG helper function and frame types, rotating the torus geometry, and starting to think about glow placement.

Now I'm working out how the rope sweeps along a closed loop, checking that skin weights blend correctly, and figuring out the right signature for the frame callback along that loop since the typing expects a void return.

Since using a function that returns a value seems risky for the along() call, I decide to instead compute positions directly by sampling the rope path at even intervals and building frames from those points with an upward normal, which feels safer than relying on along()'s own output structure.

For the collar, I set it to loop around the second neck joint with a slight lift, sweep gold tubing along it as a closed path, then scatter ten small crimson beads evenly around that collar loop, each anchored to the neck's second joint. I'm also double-checking how the rope attaches at the first neck joint, near the start of the neck's tube, to make sure that cap aligns properly with the sweep's beginning.

Rather than anchoring loops to the joints directly, I decide to use frame positions along the neck curve itself—placing the rope loop around 10% along the neck and the collar around 55%—since loops accept a frame with position and facing, which is simpler than dealing with joint planes. I keep the bead bone weighting tied to the second neck joint though.

For gold anklet rings, I plan similar loops around the leg's sweep surface near the ankle, with a thinner gold tube, applied to the front legs and lower hind legs.

For hind leg rings I'll place the ankle band a bit further along at roughly 78% of the hind chain, and add gold tail rings around 70% along the tail with a similar thin gold sweep. For the tail's color banding, I'm working out a sequence of colored bands—lavender near the base, white through the midsection, and crimson near the tip—plus a radius function that tapers from a base thickness and swells with a sine curve toward the tip.

Now I'm checking the tail plume spacing: with 9 fanned tails at wide angular spread the widths overlap too much near the base, so I'm narrowing the peak radius and angular spread so the plumes just touch rather than overlap, and adding alternating elevation offsets per tail for a staggered fan look.

I'm checking that outer tails don't clip into the hind legs given their elevation and base position — they clear it fine. I'm adding a small fluffy sphere at the tail base to hide the convergence point, and setting up the tail as a catmull-rom chain of four points swept with a radius for a tapering shape.

Writing tail point math...

Checking the tail tip height against the fox's overall proportions, I realize the total silhouette comes out too tall relative to the shoulder height, so I should scale back the final lift value to keep things proportional.

I'm sketching out the flame texture as an SVG shape with gradient colors, positioned at the tail tip facing upward, and deciding to skip extra details like orb rings or a ground shadow since this should just be the creature itself. Writing SVG flame path...

Adding swirl texture paths...

I'm placing a sphere for the head paint region, sized to make the eyes read as big anime eyes relative to the face width. Then I'm sketching a tapering muzzle sweep from the face toward the snout with a shrinking radius profile.

Now I'm adding the nose tip sphere positioned at the front of the muzzle, then sketching a lower jaw sweep that tapers from near the chin forward, checking that its radius doesn't overlap awkwardly with the muzzle's underside.

I'll skip the mouth line and instead give the jaw a cream-lavender tint for contrast, adjusting the joint positions slightly. Now I'm defining the ear joints before extrusion, setting up bone weights for the eye decals, and adding a generic helper to grab the last element of the tail joint chain for the tail-tip calculations.

Writing build function and paint logic...

Still defining the fur colors and body chain...

I'm checking the joint positions for the head and neck against the body's chest radius to make sure they connect smoothly without overlap issues.

Now I'm computing the ear and skull heights to get overall fox proportions, landing on a sizable spirit fox roughly 1.5m long with shoulder height near .78.

I'm placing seven orbiting orbs around the fox using an angular spread, giving each a glowing core and flame-card visual, and now double-checking the first orb's position puts it behind and to the left as intended.

I'm attaching the orbs and cards to the hips bone, setting up tail tuft flow vectors and randomized card variations, then finalizing the function to return the root bone. I'm also running through my import list to make sure everything (THREE, builder helpers, paint utilities, ink, zigzag, glow, etc.) is actually used, and starting to define a rope material using a striped pattern.

Now I'm detailing the ear tassel geometry—placing a thin gold rod from the ear tip down to a crimson sphere with a gold ball cap—positioned near the ear base so it peeks out from under the cheek ruff.
